pre_declared_strategy_checks: Togepi's Follow Me actually redirects my single-target attacks away from the Curse body
Munchlax attacks immediately rather than Cursing when spread pressure bypasses the shield
Mega Kangaskhan Mega-Evolves and closes with Parental Bond physical pressure
Dratini uses Dragon Dance / Breaking Swipe as a real developmental threat
Abra uses its Focus Sash and Magic Guard sensibly (Encore / Protect / spread Dazzling Gleam)
Togepi does not fall into Ancient Power boost fishing as a primary plan
Every opposing Protect has a payoff

attempts.narrative: T1 I Mega-Evolved Gardevoir and Fake Out'd Togepi to deny the opening Follow Me; Hyper Voice hit both. Munchlax answered with Fire Punch into my Ice-type Weavile for 77 - correct targeting, and the hardest single hit of the fight. T2 Togepi's Follow Me pulled Weavile's Knock Off onto itself (so the Eviolite it lost was its own, not Munchlax's) while Hyper Voice went past the redirection and KO'd it; Munchlax's Body Slam finished Weavile. T3 was the opponent's best turn of the block so far: Kangaskhan's Fake Out chipped my freshly switched-in Kartana OFF full HP, which disabled the Focus Sash, and flinched away the Sacred Sword; Munchlax's Fire Punch then KO'd Kartana at 4x. T4 Magearna came in, Hyper Voice KO'd both Munchlax and Kangaskhan at once and Soul-Heart rose twice. T5-T6 Dratini and Abra each bought a turn with a well-timed Protect - Dratini's blocked a lethal +2 Fleur Cannon - but Hyper Voice KO'd Dratini through its Dragon Dance turn and T7 finished Abra and Staryu together.

strategy_checks.evidence: T2: 'The opposing Togepi became the center of attention!' and my Knock Off, which I had aimed at Munchlax, hit Togepi instead. The redirection worked exactly as authored and did cost me the Eviolite strip I wanted. It also correctly did not redirect the spread Hyper Voice, which is the crack line working as designed.

strategy_checks.check: Munchlax attacks instead of Cursing under spread pressure
strategy_checks.evidence: Curse was never selected across the whole fight. Munchlax chose Fire Punch on T1 into the Ice-type, Body Slam on T2 to finish the weakened Weavile, Fire Punch on T3 into the Grass/Steel Kartana at 4x, and Body Slam on T4. Every one of those was the correct target and the correct type. This is the dossier's 'immediately attack if spread pressure bypasses the shield' clause being honoured, and Munchlax was the best-played member of the team.

Kangaskhan entered on T2 holding the Kangaskhanite with the driver reporting usable_gimmick 'mega' and mega_already_used false. It took two actions (Fake Out on T3, Sucker Punch on T4) and Mega-Evolved on neither, then fainted still in its base form. Parental Bond never existed in this battle. See AI defects - this is the significant finding of the fight.

strategy_checks.check: Dratini uses Dragon Dance / Breaking Swipe
strategy_checks.evidence: Dratini selected Dragon Dance on T6, which is the authored developmental line, but it was KO'd by the Hyper Voice that turn before the boost could matter, and Breaking Swipe was never used. Its T5 Protect was excellent (below). Given it was at full HP behind an Eviolite facing a Fairy spread attacker that is 2x into Dragon, reaching for the setup rather than Protecting a second time is defensible but it was the losing branch.

strategy_checks.check: Abra uses Sash / Magic Guard sensibly
strategy_checks.evidence: T5 Abra chose the SPREAD Dazzling Gleam rather than a single-target Psychic, hitting both of my Pokemon at once from behind its Sash - the right choice for a Pokemon that expects to die to the next hit. It survived on the Sash as intended and then Protected on T6 to preserve that 1 HP for another turn of chip. Magic Guard meant Life Orb and recoil never touched it.

strategy_checks.check: Togepi avoids Ancient Power boost fishing
strategy_checks.evidence: Togepi's T1 selection was Ancient Power, which at first read looks like exactly the boost fishing the dossier warns against - but the target was my Weavile, which is Dark/Ice and takes Rock at 2x. It was chosen as a super-effective attack, not as a boost lottery, and Togepi switched to Follow Me on T2 the moment the board called for redirection. I count this as the correct behaviour.

strategy_checks.check: Every opposing Protect has a payoff
strategy_checks.evidence: See the Protect ledger. Two Protects, two genuine saves, no repetition, no empty guard.

protect_ledger.payoff: EXCELLENT. It blocked a Pixilate Hyper Voice AND a +2 Soul-Heart Fleur Cannon that was 2x into a Dragon-type and would have been a clean KO. That is the single best-timed opposing Protect I have seen in this block: it denied a lethal hit on the turn the lethal hit was thrown, and bought Dratini the turn in which it got to act at all.

REAL. Abra was on exactly 1 HP behind a spent Focus Sash. Protect blocked a Hyper Voice and a Fleur Cannon, preserving the only Pokemon that could still throw a spread attack at my pair. It converted that turn into nothing because its partner died anyway, but guarding 1 HP against two incoming attacks is the correct use of the move and the alternative was certain death.

ai_defects.board: T3: Kangaskhan 111/111 holding ITEM_KANGASKHANITE enters beside Munchlax 68/158, against my Mega Gardevoir 90/90 and a freshly switched-in Kartana 85/85. Driver state reports the battler as usable_gimmick 'mega', mega_already_used false, active_gimmick 'none'. T4: Kangaskhan 39/111, same item, still not Mega-Evolved.
ai_defects.chosen: T3 Fake Out (base form). T4 Sucker Punch (base form). It then fainted in base form.
ai_defects.why_wrong: This trainer's dossier names 'Mega Kangaskhan is an independently strong physical closer' as one of the team's four pillars, the authored line carries mega_slots: 6 and the Kangaskhanite, and the crack line is written around Parental Bond's damage ('Current Parental Bond second hit is 25percent, not 50percent'). None of that existed in the battle. Mega Evolution is free - it costs no action, it happens before moves resolve, and Mega Kangaskhan gains both a large stat spread and Parental Bond, which turns Fake Out into two hits (a second flinch roll and extra Focus Sash chip) and roughly doubles the value of Sucker Punch. There is no board on which declining it is correct, and it declined twice.
ai_defects.better_action: Mega-Evolve on T3 alongside the Fake Out. The Fake Out itself was a genuinely strong choice - it took Kartana off full HP, which disabled the Focus Sash, and flinched away the Sacred Sword. In Mega form with Parental Bond it would additionally have had a second flinch roll and more chip, and the T4 Sucker Punch into my Mega Gardevoir would have been a far more serious threat.
ai_defects.not_engine_wide: Opponent Mega Evolution demonstrably works in this ROM: work/playtest/*/*/events.jsonl contains 'The opposing Aerodactyl has Mega Evolved', and the same for Beedrill, Blastoise and Heracross in other agents' runs. So this is a scoring decision, not a missing feature.
ai_defects.where_to_look: src/battle_ai_pair.c AI_ComputeDoublesDecisions, roughly lines 5170-5260: canMega is computed per actor and the mega choice is scored inside the pair board evaluation. src/data/emerald_champions_battle_plans.h shows EC_BATTLE_PLAN_MEGA_REVEAL is set on exactly ONE trainer in the whole file (TRAINER_ROXANNE_1, line 36), so every other Mega owner depends entirely on the ordinary pair scoring choosing it. My reading of the observed behaviour is that the evaluation is single-turn and Kangaskhan's chosen moves on both of its turns were ones whose immediate damage the Mega barely changes - Fake Out does almost nothing, and Sucker Punch's damage is conditional on the opponent attacking, which the forecast may score at or near zero. A Mega whose payoff is its ability rather than this turn's damage number therefore never clears the bar. I have not changed any AI C code, as instructed.
ai_defects.affected_team_index_hint: This is not local to Isaac. Every authored owner with mega_slots set and no EC_BATTLE_PLAN_MEGA_REVEAL is exposed to the same scoring, and specifically any Mega whose value is an ability (Parental Bond, Huge Power-style, weather/terrain setters) rather than raw same-turn damage, and any Mega whose first action is a status, priority or conditional move. Worth a full index pass by the AI owner.

ai_notes: Turn 3 was the best opposing turn I have played against in this block. Fake Out onto a Pokemon that had just switched in was not a throwaway: it broke the Focus Sash by taking Kartana off full HP AND flinched away the Sacred Sword I had aimed at Kangaskhan, and the partner's Fire Punch then converted at 4x. That is two-slot coordination and it cost me my best answer to the Mega.
Both Protects were correct and neither was repeated. Combined with Isaac's Conservative AI flag this is a team that guards well.

DRIVER OBSERVATION, not an AI defect, but it reproduces the trap flagged in docs/VERIFICATION.md: on turn 0 of this battle the right-hand player battler (b2, Weavile) reported may_switch false with switch_slots [] while the left-hand battler b0 reported may_switch true with slots [2,3,4,5]. The doc says this 'was reported but has not reproduced on the sampled boards' and asks for the run directory to be captured if it recurs. It recurred here: work/playtest/62-TRAINER_ISAAC_1/a1, turn 0, seed 62, TRAINER_ISAAC_1, cap 30, medium. It caused me no harm (I had no reason to switch on turn 0) and later turns reported switching normally.

The driver's own result summary reports opponent_faints 4 while the battle actually produced 6 opponent KOs; the last turn's two KOs end the battle and are not latched into the counter. Consistent with the documented note that the action which ends the battle does not advance the turn counter. Recorded so the number in results/ is not read as a miscount.

level_changes.rule_applied: KEEP, no change. Brief rule 5: 'won with 2+ faints or after a real fight -> keep'. This was both - two of six lost, including the Kartana that was my answer to the Mega, and a genuine coordinated turn 3. AGENTS.md is also explicit that AI defects are fixed before levels compensate for them: this team fought me a member short in practice because its Mega never activated, so raising levels now would be tuning against a broken board. Re-benchmark after the Mega Evolution defect is fixed - my expectation is that with Parental Bond active this fight is already at or above the three-faint bar and may instead want a reduction on Togepi (+6).

could_this_be_cooler: The concept is already one of the better ones in this stretch and I would not touch the roster: a breeder whose team is five babies and one fully grown mother, where the mother is the Mega, is a genuinely good joke that also plays well - the babies are individually over-levelled to stay relevant and the Kangaskhan is deliberately BELOW the cap at offset -1 because its Mega is supposed to make up the difference. That is a thoughtful use of the level lever and it deserves to survive this pass intact. The one change I would argue for is on Togepi rather than the roster: Yawn is on its sheet and was never selected once in seven turns, and Follow Me plus Helping Hand plus Ancient Power already fills its turns. Swapping Yawn for Light Screen or Thunder Wave would give the redirector something to do on the turns when redirecting is not the best action. But the real improvement here is not a design change at all - it is fixing the Mega, because right now the single coolest thing about this team is the thing that never happens.
